newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia corn market stable as traders eye polls.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia corn market stable as traders eye polls.

text.p: Indonesian corn prices were stable in quite trading on Tuesday, with traders expecting the run-up to the May 29 general elections to dampen sentiment.
Corn was quoted at 400 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from a week ago, on the back of ample stocks and as feedmills waited for imports to begin arriving from the first week of May.
"At least 100,000 tonnes of Chinese corn is expected to arrive from next week," one trader said. "This coupled with ample stocks are keeping the market very quiet."
Traders said they expected sentiment to be dampened ahead of the polls due mostly to currency-related factors.
"Any weakening of the rupiah will dampen sentiment, especially for imports," one trader said. "From the export point of view, it is super. From the import point of view it's hell."

The Indonesian currency sank to all-time lows last Thursday and Friday on jitters ahead of the pre-election campaigning that began last Sunday. It fell a cumulative 20 points to a historic low of 2,440.50 against the U.S. dollar last Friday.
The rupiah had recovered to 2,422.75 on Tuesday morning.
"I don't expect fresh business (imports) until after the elections because a weaker rupiah will cost importers who have to pay in U.S. dollars," the trader said.
Traders said Chinese corn was being offered at $148-$150 a tonne C&F, while U.S. and South American corn was on offer at $157-$160 a tonne for Panamax-sized shipments.
"At this time, it will make no sense for importers to look at U.S. corn," one trader said. "Chinese corn is cheaper, the sailing time is shorter and it can be bought in small quantities."
The trader said the harvest in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra was slowing down, while that in East Java were expected to begin in July.
"The Lampung harvest is almost over and players will now begin to focus on the East Java crop," he said.
The traders said soymeal prices were holding steady at 860-870 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from last week, on the back of good demand.
"Demand is steady, and is keeping prices firm," one trader said, adding that there were continued offers of Indian soymeal, but he did not have the price quotes.
